meta.analysis: blind LLM vision panel with orientation-flip position control
meta.design: 5 runs on orientation A (treated=RIGHT) + 5 runs on orientation B (horizontally flipped, treated=LEFT). Each run is an independent blind judgement; analysts received no treatment information and a neutral filename.
meta.question: Which half (LEFT/RIGHT) shows more vigorous growth (larger leaves, denser canopy, deeper green, more developed seedlings)?
meta.scoring: A run is counted as a correct treated-side identification when its chosen half equals the treated side for that orientation.
caveats: Single model family only (Claude Opus 4.8) -> 10 runs measure consistency, not cross-model independence.
n=1 photographic frame; no biological replication.
Perceptual assessment only; preliminary pixel green-canopy-cover and leaf-morphology metrics did NOT reproduce the model's stated reasons (leaf size, canopy density).

Descriptive, not causal: a content difference between trays cannot be attributed solely to the field treatment without controlled, replicated imaging (sowing density, lighting, tray position not controlled in this frame).

summary.p_value_note: Descriptive only. The 5 runs per orientation are the same model on the same frame and are NOT independent, so the nominal binomial p overstates significance. It is shown for scale/direction, not as a formal test.
summary.primary_evidence: The verdict FLIPS with the image (RIGHT in orientation A, LEFT in flipped orientation B). This excludes a fixed left-right screen-position bias; the model tracks something that mirrors with the frame (not necessarily the plants specifically -- an in-frame lighting/exposure gradient would behave the same way).
summary.not_corroborated: Preliminary pixel green-canopy-cover and leaf-morphology metrics did NOT reproduce the model's claimed canopy/size advantage; the LLM signal is perceptual and unverified.
summary.interpretation: Preliminary perceptual signal favouring the treated trays. Single model family, single frame; consistency demonstrated, cross-model independence and replication still required.
